steps.description: Charge All commits the panel's current product card / amount / stemming (ChargeStep.chargeAll, Charge.ts), and all three are reachable by click: the krackle product card selects the explosive, 3 amount increments take 5 -> 8kg and 5 stemming decrements take 2.0 -> 1.0m. The explicit [data-step="2"] click is required because the drill step above clicks [data-step="1"] manually, which disarms autoAdvance. Amount steps by 1kg (data-field="amount", clamped to the selected product's [minChargeKg, maxChargeKg]); stemming steps by 0.2m with a 0.5m floor (data-field="stemming", Charge.ts adjustStemming). Both are plain instance fields on ChargeStep with no reset path, so they carry over from the previous charge step in the same page session — asserted before each commit rather than assumed.

expect.note: command-mode trace shows bankrupt flips true here (levelEndReason: 'bankruptcy') but that is not hard-asserted at this exact step -- the earlier event's uncertain timing (step 71) could shift which 10-tick block crosses the bankruptcy grace countdown by one block either way. Asserted instead at the file's final step, where it is robust regardless: BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 consecutive ticks below the $5000 threshold (Bankruptcy.ts), and this file's cash declines monotonically with zero income sources anywhere, so the countdown that starts around tick ~76 completes by tick 200 no matter when the one weather event's extra -$8000 lands (Finding #44).

expect.note: confirms the file's own premise doesn't hold: named for worker revolt, but revolted stays false throughout -- wellBeing never gets low enough (it spends the file between 50 and 99.95, only mildly declining near the very end, nowhere near a sustained-low band; see WorkerRevolt.ts). The real, deterministic loss condition is bankruptcy: hiring 7 employees up front with zero contracts or other income anywhere in the file drains cash below the $5000 threshold around tick ~76, and BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 consecutive ticks below that threshold (Bankruptcy.ts) triggers game-over ~100 ticks later -- independent of which random events fire in between, since this file's cash never recovers once it crosses (Finding #44).
